subject: Biology
title: Cancer: Division Gone Wrong
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Cancer: Division Gone Wrong.

hook.text: Cancer starts when a cell ignores the signals that say 'stop dividing.'

buildup.text: Mutations in growth genes break the brakes. The cell multiplies without limit.

discovery.text: A tumor is a mass of rogue cells consuming resources and crowding healthy tissue.

twist.text: One mutation isn't enough. Several must accumulate—often taking years or decades.

climax.text: Chemotherapy targets rapidly dividing cells, exploiting cancer's own reckless growth.

punchline.text: Cancer is a cell that forgot how to stop.

quiz.question: What causes a cell to become cancerous?

details.summary: Cancer begins when mutations disable the checkpoints that normally control cell division. Cells multiply uncontrollably, ignore signals to stop growing, evade programmed cell death, and can eventually invade other tissues through metastasis.
details.whyItMatters: Cancer is a leading cause of death worldwide. Understanding it as fundamentally a disease of uncontrolled cell division guides treatment strategies targeting the specific mutations and pathways that drive each individual tumor.
takeaways: Cancer results from mutations that disable cell division checkpoints
Oncogenes accelerate division; tumor suppressors normally prevent it
Metastasis occurs when cancer cells invade distant tissues via blood or lymph

faq.question: How many mutations does it take to cause cancer?
faq.answer: Typically 5 to 10 key mutations in specific genes are needed. These accumulate over years, which is why cancer risk increases with age. Each mutation removes another layer of growth control until the cell divides without restraint.

faq.question: What is the difference between a benign and malignant tumor?
faq.answer: Benign tumors grow locally without invading other tissues and are usually not life-threatening. Malignant tumors invade surrounding tissues and can metastasize to distant organs through the bloodstream or lymphatic system, making them dangerous.
